text:
Vera: FYI hit a customer bug where our Node SDK retried a payment POST after a 429 and the backend eventually accepted both requests. No idempotency header used and SDK retried immediately. We should standardize behavior across SDKs and docs.

Noah: can you share the raw request/response trace? curious whether Retry-After was set or not.

Vera: trace: 
```
-> POST /api/payments
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  Content-Type: application/json
<- 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 0
  X-Trace: t_77
-> POST /api/payments
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  Content-Type: application/json
<- 201 Created
```
(no Idempotency-Key header)

Lena: Retry-After: 0 usually means the request was queued and not processed; it’s ambiguous for clients. SDKs should not rush retries for write ops without an idempotency token.

Raj: proposal for SDK defaults (short):
- Respect Retry-After when > 0 (use as delay up to cap 30s)
- If Retry-After missing/0 -> use exponential backoff with full jitter (base=200ms, factor=2, cap=5s)
- max_retries = 3 for 429 and 5xx transient errors
- Do NOT auto-retry POST/PUT/PATCH unless Idempotency header present or user enables auto_idempotency

Noah: agree. Additions: choose header name now: X-Redwood-Idempotency. SDKs may optionally auto-generate a UUIDv4 when auto_idempotency=true. Default = false while we roll it out.

Lena: server behavior checklist to pair with SDKs:
- Store idempotency records for TTL (default 24h, configurable)
- If duplicate arrives while original processing -> return 202 + operation-id (and do not re-run side effects)
- If duplicate after completion -> return stored response (status + body) so client sees canonical outcome

Vera: also: surface X-RW-Retry-Count on retried requests and log rw.retry_count/rw.retry_reason in SDK logs for debuggability.

Raj: UX note: warn loudly (single-line warn log) if user sets max_retries>0 for write ops without Idempotency header. Offer strict mode to throw error instead.

Noah: QA and tests: add integration test that simulates 429 then 201 where backend accepted first after retry; ensure when idempotency key present we only create one resource and SDK returns recorded response.

Vera: for docs/changelog blurb: 
- 429 handling: respect Retry-After header; otherwise use exp backoff + full jitter (base=200ms, cap=5s)
- max_retries=3 for transient errors
- Write requests are not retried unless X-Redwood-Idempotency present or auto_idempotency enabled
- SDKs will optionally generate idempotency keys when enabled (UUIDv4) and surface telemetry event 'sdk.auto_idempotency'

Lena: sample app request: examples-bot can you open a small repo example with Node + Python + cURL showing: set idempotency header, enable auto_idempotency, and how to handle 202 operation-id responses.

examples-bot: created examples issue #322: "safe-retries-sample" and assigned to @Raj (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/issues/322)

Raj: implementation notes for SDKs:
- flag: auto_idempotency: false by default
- when enabled attach X-Redwood-Idempotency: uuidv4() to POST/PUT/PATCH if user didn't supply one
- respect user-provided Idempotency header always
- on 429: if Retry-After>0 wait given seconds (bounded), else jittered exp backoff; stop after 3 retries
- do not retry on 4xx other than 429
- emit telemetry when auto_idempotency used and when retry prevented due to missing idempotency

Noah: also add small note in onboarding quickstart: "If your endpoint creates side-effects, include an Idempotency key or enable auto_idempotency to avoid accidental duplicates."

Vera: I'll draft the SDK CHANGELOG + a 3-line doc snippet and post PRs for Node and Python. Thanks all :thumbsup:
